Plan ahead for Great Outdoors Comedy Festival, September 11 to 13 at Erindale Park
items.summary: Residents, visitors and park users should plan for temporary closures to Erindale Park and surrounding areas starting September 6. The City of Mississauga is looking forward to welcoming the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival to Erindale Park, September 11 to 13. Visitors and residents can expect a weekend of live stand-up comedy featuring Emmy-winning and acclaimed comedians against the backdrop of the Credit River. For the first time, Erindale Park will be home to one of the largest comedy festivals in the country. m. for evening shows. Tickets are still available for all three days and can be purchased through the festival website. As Mississauga welcomes thousands of attendees to the festival, the City is advising residents, visitors and park users of temporary closures at Erindale Park and surrounding areas to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for all. To support event setup, operations and site teardown, please note these temporary changes from September 6 to 16: Dundas Street West will be reduced to one lane of traffic in each direction between Mississauga Road and Robinson Street on: A temporary crosswalk with police assistance will be available on Dundas Street West across from the main entrance to Erindale Park.

items.title: MiWay adjustments coming to Route 110 University Express starting September 7
items.summary: Customer demand drives service to support post-secondary students and general commuters between Mississauga and the Greater Toronto Hamilton Area. Serving one of Mississauga’s busiest travel corridors, Route 110 University Express will run more often starting September 7 between City Centre Transit Terminal and Clarkson GO Station. As part of this change, Route 110A University Express will be discontinued, with service merging with Route 110 University Express. The route helps students, commuters and residents travel between downtown Mississauga, University of Toronto Mississauga (UTM), the Erin Mills community and Clarkson GO Station. MiWay regularly reviews how customers use each route to match service with demand. The September 7 service changes focus on some of Mississauga’s busiest transit corridors, such as major shopping centres, regional transit hubs, post-secondary institutions and employment districts: MiWay is shifting service to where demand is high: Due to reduced ridership, MiWay is adjusting the following routes: Full route schedules are available on MiWay’s service updates page.

items.title: Ontario's Police Watchdog Opens Probe After Driver Strikes Pedestrian Mid-Disturbance Call in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CP24, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has invoked its mandate to investigate after a pedestrian was struck by a passing vehicle while police were present at a disturbance call in Mississauga on Sunday. The outlet reports Peel Regional Police Constable Tyler Bell said officers had responded to reports of two people fighting in the roadway when one of them was struck by the vehicle. According to CP24, police issued a traffic alert advising drivers of a closure on Viscount Road between Network Road and Highway 409, though the road has since reopened. The outlet reports Bell said the scene was being held as part of the investigation and that there is no threat to the community. CP24 reports Bell said he is limited in what further details he can share while the SIU's investigation into the police-involved incident continues.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows 11 Assaults a Day on Average Across Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police data shows 361 assaults were reported across the region between July 30 and August 30, averaging more than 11 incidents a day. The outlet reports the total includes 140 assaults in Mississauga, 214 in Brampton, one in Burlington, one in Caledon and two incidents in Toronto that fell under Peel's jurisdiction. INsauga reports the police data also identifies 16 hotspots where four or more assault-related incidents took place over the same period. According to the outlet, the data does not specify the type of assault involved in each case or whether victims sustained any injuries. INsauga reports the figures were compiled directly from Peel Regional Police's own incident data covering the 31-day period.

items.title: Mississauga Pesäpallo Players Set Sights on World Cup in Sydney This October
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, a Mississauga-based community group is hoping to eventually bring the Pesäpallo World Cup to the city after building a growing following for Finland's national sport locally. The outlet reports a group of Greater Toronto Area residents, some travelling from as far as Oakville and Burlington, regularly gather at Bloor Athletic Field in Mississauga to play the sport. Mississauga.com describes pesäpallo as a fast-paced game resembling baseball, featuring a distinctive field, unusual running patterns and near-constant action that appeals to players of different ages, backgrounds and skill levels. According to the outlet, while some participants treat it purely as a recreational activity, others are preparing to represent Team Canada at the 12th Pesäpallo World Cup in Sydney, Australia, running October 2 to 5 this year. Mississauga.com reports the four-day tournament is being organized by the Finnish Society of Sydney and is expected to draw teams from Australia, Finland, Canada, Germany and India competing in men's, women's and mixed categories.

items.title: Second Suspect in Cooksville Stabbing Sought for Attempted Murder, Police Warn Public Not to Approach
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, one man is in custody and a second remains at large following what police describe as a violent parking dispute that turned into a stabbing in Mississauga over the weekend. The outlet reports two men were found suffering from stab wounds and were taken to hospital with serious injuries, though their condition has since stabilized. According to CityNews Toronto, officers searched the area and arrested 30-year-old Ali Halimi of Mississauga without incident, charging him with assault. The outlet reports detectives are now searching for a second male suspect, believed to have stabbed the victims and to still be in possession of the knife, who is wanted for attempted murder. CityNews Toronto describes the outstanding suspect as Middle Eastern, approximately 25 to 35 years old, with a thin build, medium complexion, thinning brown hair and an unshaven appearance. According to the outlet, police say the suspect should be considered armed and dangerous.

items.title: Cooksville Plaza Stabbing Leaves Two in Hospital, One Suspect in Custody
items.summary: According to CTV News, two people were taken to hospital following an altercation with what police called a possible stabbing at a shopping plaza in Mississauga's Cooksville neighbourhood late Saturday afternoon. The outlet reports the incident happened near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road, just west of Hurontario Street. CTV News reports police said the two people suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries and were taken to separate hospitals, with one sent to a trauma centre. According to the outlet, paramedics described the injuries differently, saying one patient had life-threatening injuries and the other had serious, life-threatening injuries. CTV News reports investigators took one suspect into custody while continuing to work out whether any other suspects remain outstanding. The outlet reports a large police presence remained in the area, with officers advising people to avoid the vicinity.

items.title: SaiGon Pho and Grill Opens Second GTA Location Inside Square One's Food District
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto-based Vietnamese restaurant SaiGon Pho and Grill has opened a second location inside The Food District at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. The outlet reports the restaurant serves traditional Vietnamese dishes including slow-simmered pho, grilled pork rice, vermicelli bowls, banh mi sandwiches, spring rolls and grilled meats. INsauga reports the chain's first location opened near Finch Station in Toronto in 2025. According to the outlet, the new Square One location features a dine-in space finished with wood accents and soft lighting. INsauga reports the opening is part of a wave of new restaurants that arrived in Mississauga and the wider region in August, as diners look for new options heading into the fall.

items.title: Alectra delivers $25,000 in support to St. Catharines residents affected by floods
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Aug. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Alectra Inc. is providing $25,000 to Community Care of St. Catharines and Thorold to help residents manage the immediate impacts of recent flooding across the city.
